title: (L2): the symmetric-monoidal equivalence Φ^G: L Sp^G ≃ Sp is the strongest input and is only cited at §-level

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Property **(L2)** asserts that $\Phi^G$ restricts to an equivalence of symmetric-monoidal $\infty$-categories
$$\Phi^G:\ L\,\mathrm{Sp}^G\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\mathrm{Sp}$$
between $\widetilde{E\mathcal P}$-local genuine $G$-spectra and ordinary spectra, with a quasi-inverse $\Phi^{-1}$. This is the single strongest input of the proof and is used decisively in:
- Lemma geom(1),(3) — replacing equivariant mapping sets by non-equivariant ones via $\Phi^G$ on $\widetilde{E\mathcal P}$-local objects;
- the converse, geometric part (Steps G-2, G-3) — the *entire* geometric half is "transport along $\Phi^{-1}$": $Y=\widetilde{E\mathcal P}\otimes E=\Phi^{-1}(\Phi^G E)$ is presented as the image under $\Phi^{-1}$ of the connective Whitehead-tower colimit of $\Phi^G E$.

The two properties of $\Phi^{-1}$ actually used are (i) it is a genuine inverse on $\widetilde{E\mathcal P}$-local objects, and (ii) it is exact and preserves sequential colimits (so it maps the Whitehead-tower cofiber sequences and colimit to the corresponding diagram in $L\,\mathrm{Sp}^G$). These are correct and standard, but the solution provides only "[HillPrimer §6], [HHR16 §2.5.2]" with no precise statement.

**To close (for a self-contained full proof):** state (L2) as a named theorem and isolate the two used properties: that the $\widetilde{E\mathcal P}$-localized fixed-point/inflation pair gives an equivalence onto $\mathrm{Sp}$, and that the quasi-inverse is exact and preserves sequential colimits. A one-paragraph statement + a pointed reference (rather than a section-level pointer) suffices; alternatively, give the standard identification $\widetilde{E\mathcal P}\otimes\mathrm{Sp}^G\simeq\mathrm{Sp}$ via geometric fixed points and verify exactness/colimit-preservation explicitly. This is a foundational-input gap (the statement is true), not a mathematical error.
